observations.deficiency: Equipment for adequate control over air pressure is not provided when appropriate for the manufacture, processing, packing or holding of a drug product.
observations.detail: Specifically, Your firm’s re-certification program for the sterility testing suite as governed by procedure SOP#: QC- 0012 “Equipment Maintenance and Calibration”, is deficient in that the program does not outline cleanroom re-certification requirements after preventative maintenance activities to the room and/or HVAC system. On April 10" 2025, your HVAC contractor performed preventative maintenance of the sterility suite HVAC system. The sterility suite was not assessed/re-certified after the preventative maintenance to ensure that it was still operating in a state of control. On May 7", 2025, your firm observed that the Magnehilic gauge of the ISO-5 BSC utilized to conduct drug product sterility testing, was out of range during logbook review. Your investigation determined that the cleanroom pressure differentials between the ISO-7 cleanroom and ISO-7 gowning room had reversed likely due to the preventative maintenance conducted in April 2025. SOP#: QC-0012 was not updated to require room recertification after preventative maintenance activities to prevent reoccurrence.

observations.deficiency: Aseptic processing areas are deficient regarding the system for monitoring environmental conditions.
observations.detail: Specifically, Your firm’s routine environmental monitoring program for the sterility testing suite as governed by procedure SOP#: P-0023 “Environmental Monitoring of the Sterility Suite Area Clean Rooms”, is inadequate in that your alert and action limits specifications set for ISO-5 areas do not align with specifications determined in risk assessment Element-Acton-001 “Environmental Monitoring Plan and Risk Assessment for the Element-Acton Cleanroom Sterility Suite and Lab Clean BSCs at Acton, MA”. For example, per Element-Acton-001, the action level specifications for surface sample environmental monitoring excursions in the ISO-5 classified biological safety cabinet (BSC) utilized to conduct sterility testing of drug products is to be ™cFUAB)(4) plate. Procedure SOP#: P-0023 has an action excursion specification for the ISO-S sterility testing BSC for surface samples as CFU/plate. Your firm lacks scientific justification for deviating from your risk assessment Element-Acton-001.

observations.deficiency: The Quality Unit failed to ensure that the drug substance was tested and released for distribution with appropriate laboratory determination of satisfactory conformance to final specifications prior to release.
observations.detail: Specifically, [redacted] API Batch # [redacted] (Manufacturing Date: [redacted]), distributed on 22 Jun 20224, was released without meeting all required release testing specifications. The identification of [redacted] analysis, performed as part of the release testing and governed by controlled procedure Doc.# STM-3-00034, Rev. 09, Analysis of [redacted] Composition of [redacted] Using [redacted] Analyzer, Effective Date: 23 Oct 2017, was found to have yielded unreliable results. Specifically, no system suitability was performed as required by the procedure, and therefore the system suitability acceptance criterion was not met. A re-injection of the chromatogram run was subsequently performed; however, the re-injection results were not used due to standard failure, resulting in the reporting of the original results without a completed system suitability. No deviation or investigation report was generated to document or address this failure. Furthermore, the analysis was reviewed and approved by QC personnel with the system suitability incorrectly documented as having been performed and the results recorded as within acceptance criteria, neither of which was accurate. The release testing results were subsequently included in the Certificate of Analysis (COA) and the batch was approved for release by the Quality Unit on 22 Jul 2024, despite the absence of a valid system suitability and without adequate scientific justification for the acceptance of the original results.

observations.deficiency: The written stability testing program is not consistently followed, evidencing a lack of adequate Quality Unit oversight over the stability testing process and its associated controls, thereby compromising the integrity and reliability of stability data generated for drug substances and intermediates.
observations.detail: Specifically, A. The quality unit failed to ensure that stability chambers are secured, and access controlled. During the facility walkthrough conducted on 13 May 2026, the stability chambers were observed to be locked; however, they are not situated in a secure location, nor is access to them restricted. The stability chambers are located in an open area of the laboratory (Room 114), in proximity to the receiving area. As a result, all personnel granted access to the laboratory, including contractors and maintenance personnel, have direct and unrestricted contact with the stability chambers, creating the potential for unauthorized manipulation of the chambers and, consequently, compromising the integrity ofthe stability program. Furthermore, on 15 May 2026, a glass window replacement operation was performed in the laboratory. This practice further demonstrates the lack of adequate access controls surrounding the stability chambers and presentsa risk to the integrity of ongoing stability studies. B. The Quality Unit failed to ensure that stability samples were stored in a temperature-controlled or climate-controlled chamber for all studies and failed to follow controlled procedure Doc. SOP-3- 00277, Rev. 29, Stability Program, Effective Date: 20 Oct 2025. Specifically, Section 9.3 of this procedure does not define ambient temperature storage conditions as distinct from room temperature storage conditions. It is the practice of the Quality Unit, as reflected in stability protocols # PROT-3-00554, [redacted] ( [redacted] and # [redacted] - 00710, [redacted] ( [redacted] to store stability samples at ambient temperature in a locked cabinet within the QC Laboratory (Room 114 — Space” Receiving Area). This area was found to be neither temperature-controlled nor subject to temperature monitoring or review. Furthermore, controlled procedure Doc. # SOP-3-00964, Rev. 09 [redacted] Operation of [redacted] Continuous Monitoring System, Effective Date: 27 Feb 2026, does not identify Room () [redacted] 25 a location requiring a critical deviation trigger for Controlled Temperature Units (CTUs) to be monitored and reviewed. The following stability studies were found in the ambient uncontrolled temperature condition cabinet: ¢ Stability Protocol PROT-3-00554. [redacted], Lot # [redacted] ¢ Stability Protocol PROT-3-00554, [redacted] {) [redacted], Lot # [redacted] e Stability Protocol PROT-3-00554, [redacted], Lot # [redacted] Stability Protocol PROT-3-00710, [redacted], Lot # [redacted] ¢ Stability Protocol PROT-3-00395, [redacted] Lot # [redacted] C. Your Quality failed to always ensure that at least one batch per year is introduced to the stability program as required by your controlled procedure Doc. SOP-3-00277, Rev. 29, Stability Program, Effective date: 20 Oct 2025; specifically, under section 9.4.3 Annual Stability Program. This discrepancy was evident in that [redacted] —-API, Batch 4 [redacted] (Manufacturing date: [redacted] Analytical Release date: 22 Jun2024 and Commercially Release date: 6/13/2025), [redacted] manufactured [redacted] for FY2024, was not included in the stability program. In addition, this discrepancy was documented in Deviation Report # DEV-011412, opened on 23 May 2025 (QA approved 05 Jun 2025). The deviation report attributed the error to SOP-3-00721, Rev. 11 (the previous stability procedure), stating that it "does not clearly define the requirement for at least one annual batch for the stability program." However, this requirement is explicitly stated under Section 8.8.2 of the same procedure, contradicting the stated root cause. D. The Quality Unit failed to ensure that stability protocols are being followed, specifically with respect to the early removal of stability samples from climatic chambers and the timely completion of analytical testing consistent with established stability study intervals. These deficiencies are permitted under controlled procedure Doc. # SOP-3-00277, Rev. 29, Stability Program, Effective Date: 20 Oct 2025, and its predecessor, Doc. # SOP-3-00721, Rev. 12, Stability Program, Effective Date: 12 Mar 2025, as well as applicable product stability protocols. Specifically, SOP-3-00277 allows samples to be pulled early by [redacted] prior to the [redacted] interval, while SOP-3-00721 and the associated stability protocols permit early pulls of [redacted] across any interval. Neither procedure discriminates by storage conditions (i.e., [redacted]), and neither requires scientific justification or evaluation of how early sample removal may affect or impact study results, particularly during [redacted] studies. Additionally, SOP-3-00277 provides an analytical completion window of up to [redacted] after the pull-out date, rather than requiring completion within the defined stability interval, further compromising the integrity of the study timeline. Examples of early pull-out dates, late pull dates, and late interval completions were observed during the review of stability studies conducted for U.S. market products: e Stability Protocol PROT-3-00314, [redacted] API, Batch # [redacted] e Stability Protocol SLOT-3-00840, [redacted] API, Batch # [redacted] e Stability Protocol SLOT-3-00902, [redacted] API, Batch # [redacted] ¢ Stability Protocol PROT-3-00554, [redacted] =) [redacted]. Specifically, the quality unit failed to ensure that all required analytical testing intervals were performed as specified in the approved stability program. Missing analytical testing time points and/or intervals were identified across multiple stability studies mentioned in deviation reports, which compromises the ability to establish or confirm the shelf life and storage conditions of the drug product. Furthermore, it is the firm's policy [redacted] column, even for informational purposes, to demonstrate that column degradation was a contributing factor. The re- tested results were within specification, and the original OOS result was invalidated without adequate scientific justification. The root cause was not sufficiently challenged to ensure the validity of the conclusion. Additionally, no Corrective and Preventive Action (CAPA) was initiated to evaluate whether additional system suitability acceptance criteria are required to prevent recurrence. A sunilar deficiency was observed in Investigation Report # OOX-2025-004. 2. It was subsequently determined to repeat the analytical test, ensuring the sample mixture was fully dissolved, and the original OOS result was invalidated. However, no corrective action or CAPA was initiated as a result of this investigation. Furthermore, a second investigation related to the same incident was opened approximately one month later, as documented in Investigation Report # OOS-2024-0196, raising additional concerns regarding the adequacy and completeness of the original investigation. 3. Investigation Report # OOS-2025-0177, for Out-of-Specification (OOS) results obtained for [redacted] API, Batch # [redacted] disclosed an OOS result for the Related Substance test, with an unspecified impurity result of 0.12% (Limit: NM1 [redacted] The root cause was attributed to laboratory error due to contamination introduced during sample preparation. The proposed corrective action is therefore inconsistent with the findings of the investigation and does not adequately address the root cause or prevent recurrence. B. This re-evaluation was not conducted on the basis that the concurrent batch results were within specification, which does not constitute adequate scientific justification for excluding those batches from the scope of the investigation, and ensures the reliability and accuracy of the results. Furthermore, the documentation of batches involved, if any, is not required or documented as per the [redacted] software used to generate and document investigations nor required as part of the controlled procedure Doc. Your firm failed to establish laboratory controls that include scientifically sound and appropriate specifications, standards, sampling plans, and test procedures designed to assure that components, drug product containers, closures, in-process materials, labeling, and drug products conform to appropriate standards of identity, strength, quality, and purity (21 CFR 211.160(b)).
Your firm failed to conduct at least one test to verify the identity of each component of a drug product (21 CFR 211.84(d)(1)).
Your firm failed to ensure that laboratory records included complete data derived from all tests necessary to ensure compliance with established specifications and standards (21 CFR 211.194(a)).

observations.deficiency: Your quality unit failed to record, review, and approve all appropriate quality-related documents at the time activities are performed.
observations.detail: Specifically, During my inspection, I reviewed your Laboratory Cleaning Records (QAF877) for all available months in 2025 and 2026. These records are used to document laboratory cleaning activities as required by your SOP QC-W-8.22, Section 5.9, which states: " [redacted] cleaning activities shall be documented in QAF877, Laboratory Cleaning Record and reviewed [redacted] by QC Leadership." I observed the following deficiencies: a) Missing Records: Laboratory Cleaning Records for January 2025 and February 2025 were not available for review. Your management stated they suspect these records were not completed. b) Incomplete Documentation: From March 2025 through March 2026, there were numerous instances where cells were marked "N/A [initials] [date]" without adequate explanation. Your management identified these entries as indicating a lack of evidence that cleaning activities occurred.

observations.deficiency: Your firm failed to properly maintain buildings, facilities, and equipment used in the manufacture of intermediates and APIs in a clean condition, and failed to establish adequate written procedures for cleaning equipment.
observations.detail: Specifically: a) Laboratory Hood Cleanliness: During my walk through on 3/17/2026 of your laboratory facilities, I observed analytical hoods where testing is performed to be in an unclean condition. The hoods exhibited corrosion, permanent staining, flaking paint, and accumulation of residue and dust. These hoods are used for reagent preparation and analytical testing of APIs and raw materials. The condition of these hoods presents a potential risk of contamination to materials and test results. b) Inadequate Cleaning Procedures: Your SOP QC-W-8.22, "Analytical Laboratory Cleaning," does not specify approved cleaning agents or sanitizing agents for use in the laboratory. The selection of appropriate cleaning agents is left to individual chemist discretion. Your quality management stated that!{ [redacted] " an [redacted] are primarily used to clean all chemicals, but this is not documented in your written procedures.

observations.detail: Specifically: a) Outdated Cleaning Validation: Your last cleaning validation for production areas was performed in 2001, representing a 25-year gap between validations. observations.deficiency: The responsibilities and procedures applicable to the quality control unit are not in writing and fully followed.
observations.detail: Specifically, your Quality Unit (QU) failed to fulfill its duties and responsibilities. Examples include the following. a) There is a failure to conduct an appropriate investigation into out of specification (OOS) test results. There is a failure to assess and address all possible root causes for these failures and to identify and implement appropriate corrective actions to prevent their reoccurrence. b) There is a failure of the Quality Unit to review and approve all written procedures. For example, your firm uses some documents, including checklists, to supplement approved procedures that do not show review and approval (signature and date) by QA. Examples include POS206.142_R0 Lab Checklist— Data Processing for HPIC Issue Date: 27FEB2023 POS201.27_RO Issue Checklist for CoA Generation/ Checklist for CoA Review Issue Date: 14JAN2022 c) Annual product quality reviews are not being performed in a timely manner. As of the date of this inspection, your firm has not completed an annual product quality review for products manufactured in 2022. d) The annual product quality review for products manufactured in 2021 states: ’no records were found for products being tested for stability in 2021 for the Brisbane site”. The annual product quality review for products manufactured in 2020 states: “no records were found for products being tested for stability in 2020 for the Brisbane site”. These reports were approved by QA however, the lack of stability studies and stability data for 2020 and 2021 did not trigger an investigation. e) Your firm is not following SOP 206.113 Brisbane Stability Oven Operation, Rev 0 issued 088AUG2022 regarding owntoading and review of the temperature and humidity readings from the data loggers for the stability chambers. The data loggers reached their maximum storage capacity on October 6, 2022 and has not recorded temperature or humidity in the stability chambers since that date.

sections.title: Pharmaceutical quality system
sections.text: The pharmaceutical quality system (PQS) principles were adequately described in the Quality Manual. A documented system for quality assurance (QA) at the corporate level was established, with procedures covering key quality elements. The quality department, including QA and QC, was separate from the production department. Operations were documented in writing, and critical GMP requirements were essentially met. The procedures reviewed and discussed during the inspection were generally acceptable. The following major computerized systems were used by the site: S. No. …

sections.text: Manufacturing processes were clearly defined and systematically reviewed. Qualifications/validations, calibrations, and maintenance were performed in accordance with the prepared protocols and the relevant established procedures. Manufacturing steps were recorded in batch manufacturing and packaging records. BMRs and BPRs were available during the facility tour. …

sections.title: Sanitation and hygiene
sections.text: Premises and equipment were maintained at a satisfactory level of cleanliness during the inspection. Appropriate gowning was in place for staff and visitors in all areas. The company had procedures in place for personal health and hygiene.

sections.title: Qualification and validation
sections.text: The validation master plan from corporate Cipla was reviewed. One batch every 3 years was revalidated for the product manufacturing process; one batch every year was revalidated for cleaning verification; analytical revalidation was every 7 years; and equipment/utilities requalification was every 5 years. CSVs were reviewed every 3 years before revalidation. In general, the VMP was found to be adequate in covering qualification and validation activities for personnel, facilities, change control, deviations, and risk management. …

sections.text: The product complaints were classified as critical, major, or minor. A process flowchart was provided in the procedure. Complaints were handled using TrackWise. For the past three years, there have been no complaints about Artesunate suppositories 100mg. No complaint was received in 2025 related to soft gelatine capsules.

sections.title: Product recalls
sections.text: The recall procedure was in place, providing instructions for the removal of product from domestic and export markets. The procedure described the classification, level, handling, and closing of recalls. Also, a mock recall procedure was delineated. No product recall related to Artesunate suppositories 100mg took place.

sections.title: Contract production, analysis and other activities
sections.text: The manufacturing activities, including the production and analysis of Artesunate Suppositories 100mg, were carried out on-site.

sections.title: Self-inspection, quality audits and suppliers’ audits and approval
sections.text: Internal audits were performed in accordance with the SOP. Internal audits were performed based on the manufacturing site's risk and compliance rating and were recommended once every 6 months. Since the PQS was found to be generally adequate, this section was not reviewed in detail. Supplier qualification and performance monitoring were described in the procedure. In addition, another procedure titled “vendor audit management” provided guidance on the audit frequency ranging from 1 to 5 years. …

sections.title: Personnel
sections.text: The procedure for the organizational chart and job responsibilities guiding the establishment of the organization's structure was reviewed. The organization chart, along with the dedicated QA team chart, was available and presented during the opening meeting. The company had recently appointed Mr. Achin Gupta as Managing Director & Global CEO. Manufacturing (production) activities were separate from quality activities, with a dedicated supervisory and reporting pathway. …

sections.title: Training
sections.text: The SOP for training described the GMP training requirements. The Learning Management System (LMS) was used to schedule, assign, register, execute, evaluate, and record internal and external training activities. Upon review of the data integrity policy, it was noted that personnel did not receive the training before starting their on-site work. The deficiencies raised from this section have been adequately addressed, and their effective implementation will be verified during future PQ inspections.

sections.title: Personal hygiene
sections.text: The procedure for personnel health and hygiene was reviewed and found to be appropriate. All staff working at the site were subject to annual medical examinations, with the exception of visual inspectors who undergo semi-annual eye checks in order to keep them qualified for their work activities. During the visit to the manufacturing areas, hand sanitizers and appropriate gowning were provided.

sections.title: Premises
sections.text: There were three units (APIs and FPPs) at the Kurkumbh site, whereas Unit-I was relevant and covered during this inspection, as the WHO prequalified product was authorized to be produced at this unit. Facility layouts were made available. In general, premises were constructed, designed, and maintained to suit the operations to be carried out and prevent the risk of contamination of materials and products. Within Unit-I, two blocks (Pharma-I & Pharma-II) manufacture FPPs of different dosage forms. …

sections.title: Equipment
sections.text: Production equipment was of a good standard and appeared to be well-maintained. Spot checks of production balances and differential pressure gauges indicated that equipment and devices were calibrated in a timely manner. The workflow in the facility was appropriately designed, and the equipment appeared to be installed to facilitate production and reduce the risk of contamination and mix-ups. In general, most production equipment was identified by its content or purpose, with cleanliness status identified by appropriate labels. …

sections.title: Materials
sections.text: The inspector visited the warehouse located on the ground floor of Pharma I. The materials were received at the receiving bay, verified for accuracy, and accepted. A SAP checklist was used to record details of incoming material receipt. Gelatin from Gelita Germany was received on 15/05/2026. The APIs were sampled 100%, whereas excipients were sampled based on √n+1. It was noted that some excipients were sampled at 100% (such as Glycerine, PEG 6000). The sampling was carried out under RLAF, and the area was equipped with separate MAL and PAL. …

sections.title: Documentation
sections.text: Documents were designed, prepared, reviewed, and distributed in accordance with the relevant document control procedure. Documents were approved, signed, and dated, and had unambiguous content. The procedure covered all quality documents except for validation documents, which were governed by a different procedure. Procedures were reviewed regularly. QA was responsible for monitoring the periodic review of procedures. CIPDOX (a document management system) was used to prepare SOPs and specifications. …

sections.title: Good practices in production
sections.text: Production operations followed clearly defined procedures in accordance with manufacturing and marketing authorizations. Handling of materials and products, including receipt and cleaning, quarantine, sampling, storage, labeling, dispensing, processing, packaging, and distribution, was performed in accordance with written procedures and instructions, and all activities were recorded. Deviations from procedures were recorded and investigated. Checks on yields and reconciliation of quantities were carried out. …

sections.title: Good practices in quality control
sections.text: The QC function was independent of other departments. The laboratory was staffed with 96 personnel and equipped with 36 HPLCs, 4 GCs, 2 LC-MS/MS systems, 14 dissolution testers, FTIR, UV-Vis, Karl Fischer, and other equipment and instruments. The samples were received from production and the warehouse and logged into SAP, which was integrated with LIMS. The samples were allocated to trained analysts based on the competency matrix. The analytical balances were connected with LIMS, and a certificate of analysis was issued through the LIMS. …

deterministic_detail.outcome: Based on the areas inspected, the people met and the documents reviewed, and considering the findings of the inspection, including the observations listed in the Inspection Report, Oxalis Labs, located at Village Theda, P.O. Lodhimajra, Tehsil Baddi, District Solan, Himachal Pradesh, India, was considered to be operating at an acceptable level of compliance with WHO GMP Guidelines. All the non-compliances observed during the inspection that were listed in the full report as well as those reflected in the WHOPIR were addressed by the manufacturer to a satisfactory level, prior to the publication of the WHOPIR This WHOPIR will remain valid for 3 years, provided that the outcome of any inspection conducted during this period is positive.

sections.title: Pharmaceutical quality system
sections.text: The quality assurance manual provided the company’s quality policy and quality objectives and outlined the general concepts of QA, as well as the principal components or subsystems of cGMP, which were the joint responsibility of all personnel. It included Hygiene, Validation, Self-inspection, Personnel, Premises, Equipment, Materials, risk analysis, data integrity, technology transfer, and Documentation. The QA was independent of manufacturing operations and reported directly to the corporate QA. …

sections.title: Good manufacturing practices for pharmaceutical products
sections.text: Oxalis Labs manufactures the finished pharmaceutical products for Macleods Pharmaceuticals Limited. The WHO-prequalified and under-assessment FPPs were manufactured in two shared manufacturing areas: the general tablet block and the Rifa block. The change parts, filter bags, sieves, and screens were product-dedicated. Cleaning validation was performed considering solubility, maximum daily dose, PDE values, etc., and the worst case was determined. …

sections.title: Sanitation and hygiene
sections.text: An adequate level of sanitization and hygiene was observed during the inspection of various manufacturing and laboratory areas. The sanitization and hygiene covered personnel, premises, equipment, materials, and other areas.

sections.title: Qualification and validation
sections.text: The Validation Master Plan 2026 for G-Block was reviewed. The plan was prepared annually by the QA team and approved by various department heads. The VMP included personnel responsibilities for executing qualification and validation activities and providing guidance on facility qualification & validation, process validation, cleaning validation, software validation (CSV), utilities validation, analytical method validation, vendor qualification, training, etc. A separate validation master plan for the computerized system was available. …

sections.title: Complaints
sections.text: The SOP for customer complaints was reviewed. The CQA logged all complaints received in Oxalis to TrackWise before further investigation. Macleod's website provided the email addresses and phone numbers of personnel responsible for receiving the complaints. The investigation had to be completed within 5 working days for critical complaints and within 20 to 35 calendar days for major and minor complaints, respectively. Trend analysis was performed quarterly and annually. …

sections.title: Product recalls
sections.text: The procedure for product recall from the overseas market was reviewed. The recalls were voluntary and statutory. The recalls were categorized into Class I, II, and III. Mock recalls were conducted annually at the distribution level. From 2023 to December 2025, there were no recalls of WHO prequalified products. In 2026, a voluntary recall was initiated following a complaint from PAHO.

sections.title: Contract production, analysis and other activities
sections.text: Oxalis Labs is a contract manufacturer for Macleods Pharmaceuticals Limited. The WHO prequalified, and under-assessment products were manufactured on-site, while calibration, qualification, and testing for some tests were carried out at contracted sites.

sections.title: Self-inspection, quality audits and suppliers’ audits and approval
sections.text: The self-inspections were conducted following the CQA procedure once every 6-month. A checklist was used to record the areas audited. This section was not inspected in detail.

sections.title: Personnel
sections.text: From the opening meeting presentation, it was noted that the site had around 1,084 personnel on-site, in addition to contracted workers. Department No. of Employees Production 529 Quality Control 218 Quality Assurance 150 Stores 72 Engineering / EHS / Utility 75 Personnel & Administration / Account / Purchase / PPIC / Operation 28 Information Technology 08 Technical services 03 CQA 01 Total Staff 1084 The job descriptions of the site QA head, site QC manager, production head, and site operation head were reviewed. …

sections.title: Training
sections.text: A corporate SOP provided guidance on imparting training through the Performance Learning Management System (PLMS) and the manual system. The same training procedure was applied to staff and contracted workers.

sections.title: Personal hygiene
sections.text: Appropriate gowning instructions were displayed in the change rooms for the staff and visitors before entering the manufacturing and other areas. 70% IPA was used to sanitize hands. The site-specific procedure was available for personnel hygiene. The personnel working in the manufacturing areas appeared to be gowned as required, including primary, secondary, and over-gowning.

sections.title: Premises
sections.text: The general block was divided into the Rifa block, the tablet block, and the MDI block. The manufacturer also has an M block for external preparations. WHO products were manufactured in the Rifa and tablet blocks, and the following information was noted: - Rifa block has 2 dispensing booths, 1 sampling booth, 4 granulation, 1 roll compactor, 4 blending, 6 compression machines, 7 coating machines, 2 manual inspection lines, and 5 packing lines (3 blister and 2 strip packing) - Tablet block was equipped with 3 dispensing booths, 3 sampling booths, 4 granulation, 3 blending, 5 compression, 2 coat …

sections.title: Equipment
sections.text: The manufacturing facility was adequately equipped with the instruments and equipment needed to manufacture and test the FPPs. In general, the equipment was maintained adequately. The production equipment was cleaned between batches and product runs, and clean and dirty equipment hold times were established. The status labels on equipment confirmed the last cleaning date and validity.

sections.title: Materials
sections.text: The inspector visited the warehouse (general tablet), including the sampling, dispensing, quarantine, undertest, approved, and rejected/returned areas. In general, the various storage areas were well-lit, adequately maintained, and clean. The temperature mapping was performed, and hold/cold spots were identified and monitored. The temperature limit of 15-25ºC and relative humidity of NMT 60% were maintained. The environmental management system was implemented in various areas within the warehouse. …

sections.title: Documentation
sections.text: The company used an electronic document management system (DMS) to manage SOPs, specifications, and standard testing procedures. The procedures, specifications, and testing methods reviewed during the inspection appeared to be unambiguous. Responsible personnel prepared, reviewed, and approved the documents. A unique identification number was assigned and traceable across departments. Protocols and reports related to process and cleaning validation were found adequate. …

sections.title: Good practices in production
sections.text: The inspector visited the non-Rifa (white) section of the site. The site provided separate male/female changerooms and washrooms before entry to the manufacturing areas. Street shoes were removed before entering the primary changeroom, and gowning instructions were displayed on the wall for entry/exit. IPA 70% was used before entering the manufacturing areas. Operators used lockers to store their street clothes. The manufacturing area was divided into ground, first, and second floors. …

sections.text: The inspector visited the laboratory. The samples were received and stored in the SS cabinet before being assigned to the analysts for analysis. The section head maintained the competency matrix to ensure that trained analysts received the samples. The sample storage area was temperature-monitored using a calibrated thermohygrometer. The laboratory has 218 staff, including 17 microbiologists. The laboratory was equipped with 61 HPLCs (Shimadzu, Agilent, and Thermo Fisher) and 7 GCs using Chromeleon 7.2 software. …
